paper_metadata.title: Laser powder bed fusion of an ultrafine microstructural in-situ TiB2/Al composite with excellent mechanical properties and thermal stability at elevated temperatures

evidence.quote: In this study, an in-situ TiB2 particle reinforced Al–Cu–Mg–Fe–Ni (Al2618) alloy was additive manufactured by laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) with excellent printability.

An Al–Cu–Mg–Fe–Ni (Al2618) alloy reinforced with TiB2 particles was fabricated via the in-situ mixed salt-metal reaction, as described in previous work [34]. The composite ingot was subsequently gas-atomized into TiB2-decorated composite feedstock powders.

With the optimized L-PBF processing parameters, crack free and near fully dense bulk samples (a relative density of ~98.5 %) were built up for further mechanical property tests and microstructure characterizations.

parameters.atmosphere: flowing argon (Ar) atmosphere with oxygen below 0.02 vol%

other.scanning_strategy: laser scanning direction alternated by 67° between consecutive layers

evidence.quote: The L-PBF was conducted by a TruPrint 1000 metal 3D-printing machine equipped with a 200 W fiber laser with a spot size of 30 μm under a flowing argon (Ar) atmosphere. The proportion of oxygen was maintained below 0.02 vol %. The laser scanning direction was alternated by 67° between the consecutive layers without the preheating of the Al baseplate. The hatching distance and the layer thickness were set as 100 μm and 30 μm, respectively. The scanning power and velocity were optimized as 170 W and 1000 mm/s, respectively
To evaluate the heat resistance of the L-PBF composites, some of the as-printed samples were subjected to thermal exposure in the furnace at 190 °C and 300 °C for up to 150 h.
